1.

This is the first petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking grant of regular bail to the petitioner
in the case bearing Fir No. 212 dated 10.08.2022 registered under Sections 408, 420 of the Indian
Penal Code (Sections 120-B, 465, 467, 468, 471 Ipc added later on) at Police Station Division No. 6,
Ludhiana.

2.  The present FIR was lodged on the allegations that the the petitioner was working as a Manager with the complainant since 19.01.2017 and after hatching a criminal conspiracy with other co-accused to cheat the complainant, he siphoned funds of Rs. 10 lacs from the bank account of the complainant and obtained wrongful benefit for himself.

The complainant conducted an internal audit and on subsequent review of the bank account statement of the complainant, it is found that the petitioner had transferred a total sum of Rs. 13,64,250/- by various transactions from the complainant's current bank account maintained with the ICICI Bank having Branch at Feroz Gandhi Market, Ludhiana.

During investigation the investigating agency found that a total sum of 2023.12.18 19:25 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this order/ judgment Chandigarh 2023:PHHC:162268 Rs.
6,06,00,000/- have been infact siphoned of and the funds of the company were transferred in the bank account of parents and siblings of the petitioner.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner inter alia contends that the petitioner has been in custody for the last more than nine months and the offence under which the FIR has been registered is triable by the Magistrate.

The co- accused have already been granted regular bail by learned Additional Ramakant Jha vs State Of Punjab on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185475748/
1 Sessions Judge, Ludhiana on 27.10.2022 (Annexure P-11).

entities.text: Additional Ramakant Jha vs State Of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has been made a scapegoat and no discrepancies were found in the audit report.
The entire case of the prosecution is based upon documentary evidence, which is already on record.

4. Per contra, learned senior counsel for the complainant has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the petitioner on the ground that infact the pleadings of the petitioner in para 'H' at page 10 would indicate that he has admitted his guilt and the material witnesses have not been examined so far.
As such the release of the petitioner would impede the progress of the trial and there is every likelihood that he would influence the witnesses.

5. Per contra, learned State counsel opposes the grant of bail to the petitioner on the ground that sufficient material is available on record to indicate the complicity of the petitioner in the present case and the petitioner is accused of siphoning of huge amount of more than six crores.

6. A two Judge Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in 'Satender Kumar Antil v. CBP' (2022) 10 SCC 51,
with respect to prevailing conditions of undertrial prisoner in India has observed:
"6. fails in India are flooded with undertrial prisoners.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBP' (2022) 10 SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The statistics placed before us would indicate that more than 2/3rd of the inmates of the prisons constitute undertrial prisoners.

Of this category of prisoners, majority may not even be required to be arrested despite REENA 2023.12.18 19:25 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this order/ judgment Chandigarh REENA 2023.12.18 19:25 2023:PHHC:162268 registration of a cognizable offence, being charged with offences punishable for seven years or less.
They are not only poor and illiterate but also would include women.
Thus, there is a culture of offence being inherited by many of them.

As observed by this Court, it certainly exhibits the mindset, a vestige of colonial India, on the part of the investigating agency, notwithstanding the jact arrest is a draconian measure resulting in curtailment of liberty, and thus to be used sparingly.

In a democracy,
there can never be an impression that it is a police State as both are conceptually opposite to each other."
7.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusing the record, it transpires that the petitioner was initially arrested on 12.09.2022 and thereafter released on interim bail by this Court and he has been in custody for more than nine months.
The investigating agency has already completed the investigation and filed the final report on 07.12.2022.
The trial of the case has not made any progress as out of 27 prosecution witnesses cited, none has been examined till date.
Keeping the petitioner in further detention without the prospect of the trial being concluded in the near future, would be violative of his rights under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

8. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and the petitioner- Ramakant Jha is ordered to released on regular bail, subject to his furnishing bail bonds/surety bonds to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Chief Judicial Magistrate/Duty Magistrate.
